nodes.text: A steady current of 2.5 A is created in a wire for 1.0 minute. How much charge passed by any given point, and how many electrons would this be?

nodes.spoken_math_alternative: I equals Q divided by delta t; therefore I equals 2.5 coulombs per second, which equals Q divided by t.
Q equals I times t, which equals 2.5 coulombs per second times 60 seconds, or 150 coulombs.
N equals 150 coulombs times one electron per 1.6 times 10 to the negative 19 coulombs, which equals 9.4 times 10 to the 20 electrons.
n equals 9.4 times 10 to the 20 electrons times one divided by 6.022 times 10 to the 23 electrons per mole, which equals 0.0016 mole.

nodes.detailed_figure_description: A closed rectangular circuit has a battery on the left labeled V, with its positive terminal marked, and a zigzag resistor on the right labeled R in orange. Electron symbols, e⁻, and arrows around the wire show electron motion from the battery along the bottom toward the right, upward past the resistor, leftward across the top, and downward toward the battery.
nodes.figure_alternative: Closed battery-and-resistor circuit showing electron flow around the wire.
The resistor circuit symbol: R followed by a zigzag line. An arrow labels it “circuit symbol.”

nodes.spoken_math_alternative: The units of ohms equal volts per ampere, which equal joules per coulomb divided by coulombs per second.

nodes.text: A resistor resists the flow of current.
They're often used to limit current in a part of a circuit. Wires themselves have some resistance, but we'll usually ignore it.
